source.title: VisualScratchpad: Inference-time Visual Concepts Analysis in Vision Language Models
source.authors: Hyesu Lim; Jin-Ho Choi; Taekyung Kim; Byeongho Heo; Jaegul Choo; Dongyoon Han

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAEs and latent interventions as tools for analyzing VLM behavior, but does not test superposition, capacity pressure, or the claim versions’ representational geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper cites superposition and discusses neurons responding to multiple concepts as motivation for SAEs, but reports no test of overlapping directions, feature sparsity or importance, capacity competition, or feature dimensionality. Its own results concern visual-concept inspection and interventions in VLMs. Those findings are recorded as none because they do not measure a claim version.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs on a CLIP vision encoder as a tool for debugging VLM answers. Its results are illustrative case studies of concept ablation and steering. It reports no test of superposition geometry, capacity competition, causes of polysemanticity, distributed features in LLMs, SAE completeness or stability, or feature dimensionality. Polysemanticity is cited (Elhage et al., 2022) only as motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors present VisualScratchpad, an interface that links vision-encoder SAE concepts to text tokens via attention. Through case studies they show VLM failures can stem from limited cross-modal alignment, misleading concepts, or unused hidden cues.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains SAEs on CLIP vision-encoder activations and uses attention-linked visual concepts and latent ablations in a VLM; it does not use or reproduce the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The SAE is trained on CLIP-ViT-large layers 2, 6, 10, 14, 18, and 22; case studies use layer 18. The paper states that layer choice corresponds to different levels of visual concept complexity. The Case 2 steering is performed over two iterative rounds.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating attention-linked clusters of vision-encoder SAE latents removes the corresponding caption topics while leaving unrelated content (qualitative, one example).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clusters of vision-encoder SAE latents can causally control corresponding content in VLM outputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating or amplifying selected visual SAE concepts flips VLM answers in single illustrative cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering vision-encoder SAE concepts can change a VLM's chosen interpretation.

fits_no_version.finding: Rephrasing a question to name a cue the encoder already captured corrected the answer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: VLM errors can stem from poor alignment between captured visual concepts and text tokens.

record.peer_reviewed: ICLR 2026 Workshop: Principled Design for Trustworthy AI
record.problems: Evidence on VLM behavior consists of a small number of illustrative case studies, with no reported quantitative evaluation, uncertainty estimates, or control conditions. The paper itself notes that the interface is intended for interactive analysis and does not directly scale to large automated experiments.

untested.parts: All parts: no toy model, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
All parts: no capacity or importance analysis.
All parts: no analysis of the causes of polysemanticity.
All parts: the SAE is on a CLIP vision encoder, and no measure of feature distribution or recovery quality is reported.
Completeness, stability and canonicity are not measured. The paper notes that latents vary in granularity and can be hierarchical or correlated, citing others, but tests none of this.
All parts: no comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: This is a workshop tool paper with three qualitative case studies plus one caption-ablation example. It has no quantitative evaluation or controls. The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition only as motivation for SAEs, so no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network test of overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
No test of capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or shared dimensions for others.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity indicates superposition.
The SAE is trained on a CLIP vision encoder; the paper does not test whether LLM activations are distributed across neurons or whether an SAE recovers their features.
Latent interventions test some causal effects, but the study does not establish SAE features as complete, stable, or canonical units.
No test compares one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: LLaVA-Next-8B
rows.operation_detail: Rephrased the question to mention a hand with a mitten.
rows.measure: Answer to whether the cup is on a surface or a hand
rows.baseline: Incorrectly answered that the cup was on a surface.
rows.value: After the question was rephrased to mention a hand with a mitten, the model answered correctly.
rows.note: The authors report that glove-related visual concepts were active and that the attention map attended to the hand. The prompt change is evidence about cross-modal alignment, not superposition or the listed claim versions.
rows.check: A prompt-rephrasing case study of VLM cross-modal alignment; it does not measure any claim version. It also does not belong as an SAE intervention row.

rows.subject: LLaVA-Next-8B
rows.operation_detail: Removed activated concepts related to a wheelchair and sitting.
rows.measure: Answer to whether an elderly person is sitting or standing
rows.locator: Section 3, Case 2; Figure 3; Appendix A.5, Figure 10
rows.note: The paper says the concepts were removed over two iterative rounds; it does not report a numerical effect.
rows.check: A single illustrative concept-ablation case of the authors' own tool, with no rate or control. It does not bear on any version, so 'observed' has no claim referent.

rows.subject: LLaVA-Next-8B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated duck-related latents and amplified rabbit-related latents.
rows.baseline: Initially described a duck; rabbit-related concepts were also activating.
rows.note: The removal and amplification are reported together as the intervention.
rows.check: A single illustrative steering case of the authors' own tool. It does not bear on any version.

rows.subject: LLaVA-Next-8B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the latent cluster associated with the shark topic.
rows.measure: Generated caption content associated with the ablated cluster
rows.baseline: Original caption included the associated topic.
rows.value: The authors report that ablating each topic cluster removes its associated portion of the caption while leaving unrelated content intact.
rows.note: The paper describes four major caption topics and corresponding clusters; this row records the shark ablation shown in the figure.
rows.check: A qualitative demonstration of cluster ablation in the authors' method (Fig. 7). It is not a measure of any version.
